clauses.clause: Sole sentence, part 1: James B. Horigan may be retained in the Forest Service with his present excepted status
Sole sentence, part 2: he may be paid from the statutory position of law clerk

data_errors: The slice's title and wpa_summary say 'without regard to Civil Service Rules'; the held transcription has no such words and says only 'may be retained in the service with his present excepted status'.
The slice's title has run-together words ('eligiblefor', 'hissalary', 'ex cepted') and is cut off.
The slice's president field is empty; the held transcription names William H. Taft.
The slice's type_lead class 'spent' has no performance source behind it; rule (e) requires one.

gaps.what: An accepted original printing of EO 1365. The transcription's citation '1911 CSR 112' appears to point to page 112 of the Civil Service Commission's annual report covering 1911; that reading is not confirmed.
gaps.where_to_look: U.S. Civil Service Commission annual report for 1911, p. 112 (HathiTrust, Google Books or the print volume); ProQuest replica of the State Department copy. A Monthly Catalog entry for the order appeared in search results (mocat.library.unt.edu/catalog/198-ch518) but was not opened.

gaps.what: Performance and end of the permission: whether Horigan was in fact retained, and the date of his separation from the Forest Service or his death.
gaps.where_to_look: Official Register of the United States 1911 and 1913 (Department of Agriculture, Forest Service); Department of Agriculture personnel records at the National Archives (NPRC official personnel folder).

gaps.what: Whether any later instrument expressly revoked or superseded EO 1365. The slice lists none and the web searches surfaced none; no dedicated search for one was run.
gaps.where_to_look: Later Civil Service Commission annual reports; CIS Index to Presidential Executive Orders and Proclamations.

moves.note: Only a Wikisource transcription is held. Two standard web searches found no official printing; the transcription cites 1911 CSR 112, which was not located online.

propositions.claim: The transcription gives the order as a one-sentence permission to retain one named person and pay him from the law clerk position (lead only, not an original).
propositions.quote: Mr. James B. Horigan, an expert in an excepted position in the Forest Service, Department of Agriculture, may be retained in the service with his present excepted status

propositions.claim: The transcription attributes the order to Taft, dated May 29, 1911, and cites a printing at 1911 CSR 112.
propositions.quote: Signed by President William H. Taft Monday, May 29, 1911 1911 CSR 112

searches: Web (standard): Horigan + Forest Service + 'may be retained in the service' + 'law clerk' + 1911 Civil Service Commission annual report; returned only a Wikisource mirror and Monthly Catalog entries
Web (standard): 'James B. Horigan' Forest Service law clerk; returned only the Wikisource mirror, no biographical or service record

review.conclusion_reason: OPEN and formal status unknown are warranted: the available evidence establishes neither performance or another ending nor continuing operation at the cutoff. The result names the missing original, performance/separation/death evidence, and later-instrument evidence. The absence of an accepted original prevents T2 and all higher tiers.
missed_evidence: The held file’s title explicitly says ‘Authorizing Retention of James B. Horigan in Forest Service Without Regard to Civil Service Rules.’ Thus the data_errors assertion that the held transcription has ‘no such words’ is false as written, although those words are absent from its operative sentence. This does not decide operative status.
review.stop_code_verdict: wrong (ONLY_COMPILED_TRANSCRIPTION_FOUND fits the first gap: the slice identifies a held transcription and original_not_usable:mirror_transcription; NOT_FOUND fails to distinguish that evidence from no text found)

verdicts.reason: The named file contains the quoted retention permission and continues: ‘and paid from the statutory position of law clerk.’ It is a Wikisource transcription, not an accepted original.

The file explicitly gives ‘Signed by President William H. Taft Monday, May 29, 1911’ followed by ‘1911 CSR 112’; the signature and date also appear beneath the operative sentence. This confirms the attribution and citation, not the identity of the cited publication.

stop_code_verdict: wrong (ONLY_COMPILED_TRANSCRIPTION_FOUND fits the first gap: the slice identifies a held transcription and original_not_usable:mirror_transcription; NOT_FOUND fails to distinguish that evidence from no text found)
